description: We SEVVIYAN, believe every unanswered question is an opportunity to explore beyond boundaries. Driven by curiosity for space, united by science and strengthened by teamwork, we continuously learn, research and innovate as ONE team. Like an endless journey of discovery, we keep questioning, improving and exploring until curiosity turns into meaningful impact.
summary:
Every landscape has a story written in its rocks, sediments and terrain. Some of these stories, hidden across Earth, may hold clues to understanding another world — Mars.

SEVVIYAN brings these two worlds into one journey of exploration. It is an Earth–Mars comparative research platform that investigates how terrestrial landscapes can help us understand Martian geological environments. Using open-access satellite imagery, elevation models, geological studies and NASA planetary datasets, the project explores terrain morphology, sedimentary features, mineralogical indicators and surface characteristics to uncover meaningful similarities and differences.

Through an interactive web application, SEVVIYAN transforms complex planetary data into accessible comparative reports, connecting landscapes on Earth with distant terrains on Mars. More than a visual comparison, it encourages us to look beyond appearances, question geological processes and discover how our own planet can serve as a natural laboratory for planetary exploration.

"Because understanding another world may begin by learning to read the stories written on our own."
details:
PROBLEM APPROACH

Understanding Martian geological environments through orbital observations alone can be challenging. Identifying suitable terrestrial analogues also requires comparing multiple geological, topographical and environmental parameters rather than relying on visual similarities.

SEVVIYAN is an Earth–Mars comparative research platform that investigates terrestrial environments, particularly Theri Kaadu (Kuthiraimozhi, Tamil Nadu), Ounianga Lakes,(Chad , Sahara),Hamoun Basin(Iran , Afghanistan),Lake Turkana(Kenya , Ethiopia)alongside selected Martian regions such as gale crator,bangold dunes,jezero crator. It uses satellite observations, geological research and planetary mission datasets to examine similarities, differences and the scientific relevance of these environments.

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT APPROACH

We followed a data-driven research approach:

Earth Data Collection:

Gathered satellite imagery and geographical information from Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Copernicus DEM, MODIS and ASTER, wherever suitable data were available.

EXAMPLE: THERIKAADU,KUTHIRAIMOZHI.

Figures: Sentinel-2 L2A True Colour Composite (B4/B3/B2) of the Kuthiraimozhi Teri dune complex (Sevviyan AOI, Tamil Nadu, India; acquisition window: Jan 1 – Jun 30, 2026), showing the reddish-orange iron-stained aeolian sand body bordered by green agricultural fields.| Sentinel-2 L2A False Colour Composite (B8/B4/B3) highlighting surface feature differentiation between exposed Teri sand deposits and surrounding vegetation.| Sentinel-2 L2A Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR) Composite (B12/B8A/B4) revealing substrate and moisture-related spectral contrasts across dune crests and interdune corridors.|  Sentinel-2 L2A Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) illustrating sparse vegetation cover across the central sand complex relative to irrigated surroundings

Mars Data Collection:

Explored NASA mission datasets, including CTX, HiRISE, CRISM, THEMIS and MOLA, alongside available rover observations.

EXAMPLE: GALE CRATOR,MARS

Figure 1: MRO Context Camera (CTX) Regional Mosaic of Gale Crater and Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), establishing the basin-scale geomorphological context of the Bagnold Dune Field.

Figure 2: MRO HiRISE High-Resolution Orbital View detailing dark-toned aeolian sand accumulations and stratified mound flanks along northwestern Mount Sharp.

Figure 3 : Mars Global Surveyor MOLA Colour Hillshade & Topography illustrating the regional elevation gradient across Gale Crater, from the deep northern crater floor (blue) to the elevated southern rim and central mound.


Geological Investigation:

Studied terrain morphology, aeolian processes, sedimentary environments, elevation, surface characteristics and mineralogical evidence.

Comparative Analysis:

Used Gemini AI-assisted analysis to organise and investigate Earth–Mars datasets, identify potential geological relationships and support comparative research.

Digital Development:

Transformed the research into an interactive web platform with visual content, location information and comparative research reports.

COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT & PROJECT IMPACT

What We Hope to Achieve

Our goal is to make planetary science and Earth–Mars analogue research more accessible to students, educators, researchers and space enthusiasts through an interactive, data-driven platform.

Benefits & Intended Impact

1. Encourages students to explore planetary science using real scientific datasets.

2. Highlights the potential research value of terrestrial landscapes, including Theri Kaadu.

3. Makes complex Earth-observation and Mars mission information easier to understand.

4. Promotes the use of open-access scientific data for educational and research purposes.

5. Inspires young innovators to participate in planetary exploration and scientific discovery.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

• Research & Data Sources

• NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)

• NASA Mars mission archives

• USGS EarthExplorer

• Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem

• NASA Earthdata

• Arizona State University Mars image explorers

• Published geological research papers

PROJECT INNOVATION

The creative aspect of SEVVIYAN lies in connecting different worlds through publicly accessible scientific information. Instead of treating Earth and Mars as separate subjects, the project uses terrestrial geological environments as research opportunities to investigate Martian surface processes.

By combining planetary datasets, AI-assisted research workflows and interactive web development, we transform complex scientific information into an accessible comparative experience.

CREDITS AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

We sincerely acknowledge NASA, ESA, USGS, the Copernicus programme, Arizona State University and the wider scientific community for providing open-access datasets, mission observations and research resources. We also acknowledge the developers of the AI platforms and digital tools that supported our research, development and presentation process.

USE OF AI

  • ChatGPT - video content, research organising and content structuring.
  • Google Gemini - Earth–Mars data comparison data analysis, research interpretation and video-generation.
  • Google LLM - Generating visual video content for project presentation.
  • Lovable AI - Frontend development and interactive website creation.
  • Canva AI - Video editing, visual design.
